item.name: TaxiGo

request.description:
Signs in a **customer** and returns the API token used by every ride request.

Set the collection variables `username` (email or phone) and `password` first. The test script saves the token into `{{token}}` automatically.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| username | yes | Email or phone number |
| password | yes | |
| device_name, device_os, device_model, fcm_token, app_version | yes | Device details. Postman sends fixed test values |

`device_name` includes the username: the API stores one device row per device name, so a shared name would move device rows between accounts.

request.description:
Both airports with everything the app needs to build the booking screens. **No login needed.**

- `zones`: fare per zone (A–D), each with its `neighbourhoods`. The passenger picks a neighbourhood; its zone sets the price.
- `interurban`: flat fares from the airport to other towns.
- `night`: night window in Cameroon time and the surcharge added to any pickup inside it.
- `vip`: hourly rate and minimum hours (VIP hire is enabled in V1.1).

All amounts are whole **XAF**. Fares are edited in the Dashboard (TaxiGo → Tariffs) and the app reads them here, so no app update is needed when prices change.

The test script stores `hub_id` (Douala), `neighbourhood_id` (Bonamoussadi, zone B) and `destination_id` (Yaoundé → Kribi) for the next requests.

response.name: Douala and Yaoundé Nsimalen

request.description:
Calculates the fare **before** booking. **No login needed.** The same calculation runs again when the ride is booked, so the price cannot be changed by the app.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| hub_id | yes | Airport from `01` |
| trip_type | yes | `airport_to_city`, `city_to_airport`, `interurban` (`vip_hourly` in V1.1) |
| neighbourhood_id | for city trips | Sets the zone and the price |
| interurban_destination_id | for `interurban` | |
| is_scheduled | no | `true` to book for later. Default: as soon as possible |
| pickup_at | if scheduled | ISO 8601, at least 30 minutes ahead, at most 30 days |

`is_night` is `true` when the pickup falls inside the airport's night window (Cameroon time); `night_surcharge` is then added.

response.name: Scheduled night pickup, zone B (+ night surcharge)
As soon as possible, zone B
Error: no neighbourhood, pickup too soon

exec: // Scheduled pickup: tomorrow at 23:30 Cameroon time (inside the night surcharge window)

request.description:
Books a ride. **Login required.** The ride starts as `pending_payment` and is confirmed only after payment (`06`).

Same fields as the quote, plus:

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| location.address | for city trips | The city-side point: drop-off for `airport_to_city`, pickup for `city_to_airport` |
| location.lat, location.lng | no | Map pin. Optional until Google Maps is live |
| flight_number | no | Shown to the driver. Upper-cased |
| passenger_name, passenger_phone | no | Default to the signed-in customer |
| notes | no | Max 500 characters |

The airport side of the trip is filled in automatically. The test script stores the ride reference in `{{ride_ref}}`.

Unpaid rides expire after 60 minutes.

Booked: interurban Yaoundé → Kribi

request.description:
The signed-in customer's rides, 20 per page (`?page=2` for more).

| scope | Shows |
|---|---|
| `upcoming` | Rides being searched for or in progress, and unpaid rides from the last hour |
| `past` | Completed, cancelled and expired rides |
| *(none)* | Everything, newest first |

response.name: Upcoming
Past

request.description:
One ride. The app calls this every 5 seconds while waiting for payment, and during the ride for the status and the driver's position.

**Ride statuses:** `pending_payment` → `searching` (paid, finding a driver) → `assigned` → `en_route` → `arrived` → `on_board` → `completed`. Also `cancelled` and `expired`.

`driver` and `vehicle` are `null` until a driver accepts the ride. `can_pay` and `can_cancel` tell the app which buttons to show.

response.name: Waiting for payment
Paid, finding a driver

request.description:
Sends the payment request to the payer's phone. The customer approves it with their PIN; then poll `05` until `payment.status` is `paid` (up to 2 minutes).

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| method | yes | `mtn_momo` or `orange_money` |
| phone | yes | The number that pays, e.g. `677000111` |

⚠️ **On the staging server this sends a real payment request** to the number given. Use your own number and a small test fare.

A new request is refused while the previous one is still waiting (about 2½ minutes).

Error: a request is already waiting

item.description:
# TaxiGo customer API

Airport transfers at **Douala (DLA)** and **Yaoundé Nsimalen (NSI)**. Fixed fares, 100% cashless (MTN MoMo, Orange Money).

## Booking flow
1. `01` Load airports, zones and fares
2. `02` Show the fare (optional)
3. `03` Book the ride → status `pending_payment`
4. `06` Send the payment request to the customer's phone
5. `05` Poll the ride until it is paid → status `searching`

Run the requests in order: scripts save the token, IDs and ride reference into collection variables.

## Responses
Every response has `status` (`true`/`false`). Success: `data`. Errors: `message` (ready to show to the user) and, for invalid fields, `errors` per field.

| HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 / 201 | OK / created |
| 401 | Not signed in or token expired |
| 404 | Not found (or not this customer's ride) |
| 422 | Invalid data, or action not allowed in this state |
| 429 | Too many requests |

Times are ISO 8601 in Cameroon time (`+01:00`). Amounts are whole XAF.
